items.note: In the black footer the field gets a red danger border, and below it sits a small red error icon with a plain sentence in footer text. The pink submit sits flush against the field, as in reference 06. All three samples agree. It reads clearly. The only departure is that the submit is a worded pink button where the reference uses a square arrow button.

This matches light mode, as rule 10 intends. The band, stickers and white on-footer field stay the same, the CTA turns pink as in reference 11, and the danger border and message stay readable on black. The hero and the footer meet with a clear seam.

The footer stacks the headline, the field with its danger border, the pink submit and the error line at full width, the way reference 10 stacks its black footer. It is easy to read on a phone and nothing breaks.

The form gives way to a white ink-framed panel holding a die-cut word badge (two samples show joined and done, the third shows thanks) next to one confirmation sentence. That is the spec's success-badge register, and it is a framed outcome, as the reference would build one. The badge is small but well drawn, with a condensed word on an ink slab.
The same white on-footer panel and badge are kept in dark, so the outcome still stands out on the black footer. The chrome inverts as in reference 11 and the bands do not change.
On the phone, the success panel fills the full width of the black footer, with the badge above the sentence. It reads at a glance and keeps the reference's drawn panel language.

Each sample shows a dashed white empty box with one drawing of the missing thing (a folder or a page stack), one sentence, a hint and an outline Clear filters button. That is the reference 06 dashed box with a sticker added. The focused field has the pink halo and ink ring. Two things fall short: the field's clear glyph is navy, and in one sample the page-stack drawing is small and thin.

The empty box becomes a raised dark-grey field with a faint dashed edge and keeps its colour drawing. The lemon hero, the pink CTA and the white field on the band all follow reference 11. It is clear, but the dashed edge is softer than in light.

The dashed empty box, drawing and Clear filters button fit the phone width well. Above them, the hero's lower stickers sit chopped by the bottom seam, some of them about half gone. The tag pills wrap onto two loose rows. Reference 09 crops its stickers more cleanly and keeps its rows tighter.

The focused current nav pill gets a 2px ink ring with an offset, like the focus-visible frame in reference 05. The hero behind it is the reference's own composition: a 96px headline, a black CTA with a bordered search at one height, and thick ink stickers cropped at the side edges.

The focused current pill turns white with a white offset ring on the black bar, the CTA goes pink, and the band and stickers stay as in light. This matches reference 11 closely, and the focus is easy to find.

The menu button shows a clear double ink focus ring. The hero stacks a full-width CTA and search. The two lower stickers are cut by the band's bottom seam, about half showing, which is weaker than the clean edge cropping in reference 09.

The hero and card vignettes are mostly thick die-cut stickers in the 01 and 03 manner: flat band fills, an even ink outline and solid lower strips. They include a pad with a page stack, a book, a mug, an envelope, a flag and a bell, each different. A few do not read as anything: a striped teal disc with a black blob, and a notched marigold slab used as the featured post's art.

Article figures and related-post vignettes are full thick stickers centred on band grounds: a keypad board, a puzzle piece, a clipboard, a ruler, a pad and a flag. The strips are deep and the outlines even. Each one is its own object, at the reference's sticker craft.

The drawings fit the topic well (a clipboard, open pages, a megaphone, a parcel, a ruler, a clock) and are built as thick board with solid strips. One sample repeats the ambiguous striped disc from the home page, but the rest read clearly.

Each sample now has its own about drawing (an ink bottle, a speech bubble or a page stack) on a periwinkle ground, with a solid strip and an even outline. The rc.4 gap, where the page reused a card vignette, has closed.

Only the hero stickers carry motion: ft-drift, linear and bound to scroll, so they hold still in a capture taken without scrolling and nothing moves on load. That is the reference's sparse, paper-like motion, as the spec describes it.

findings.summary: On phones, the hero's lower stickers sit on the band's bottom seam with only about half of each showing, and they read as chopped objects. Reference 09 crops a sticker at a side edge or lets it cross the seam while most of it stays visible.

Two details break the ink-on-white palette and the sticker scale. The search field's clear glyph is navy-blue rather than ink. In one sample the empty-state drawing is a small, thin page stack, well below a medium sticker's weight. The reference keeps every glyph ink, and its states use drawings at full sticker weight. The navy glyph was also noted in rc.4 and is still open.

A few vignettes do not read as an object: a striped teal disc with a black blob, and a notched marigold slab as the featured post's art. The reference's stickers (coins, receipts, tools) can each be named at a glance.
